review_scope_note: Full-repository audit; the signing reviewer verified the arithmetic underpinnings (prime counts, breakdown table) and the source code's existence, and checked for run artifacts.
verification_methods: Sieve computation: pi(17,389) = 2,000 exactly and 17,389 is prime — the '2,000 primes up to p=17,389' framing is arithmetically exact
Confirmed scripts/experiments/zaremba-transitivity/check_transitivity.cu exists and is the only artifact in that directory — no run log is committed

Reviewed the revised Dickson argument for internal soundness (Borel/Cartan eigenline exclusions, the resultant-based exceptional exclusion with prime set {2,3,5,11,19,29,31,41,59} all < 61) and the page's determinant caveat

claim_reviews.claim: Computational check: the semigroup acts transitively on (Z/pZ)^2 \ {0} for each of the first 2,000 primes (p <= 17,389), 133 s wall time, zero non-transitive cases.
claim_reviews.evidence: The arithmetic frame is exact (pi(17,389) = 2,000, verified by sieve; breakdown table sums correctly) and the source code exists with the described CUDA/CPU split, but no run log or output artifact is committed. The claim is cheap to reproduce (O(p^2) per prime) and highly plausible; it is simply not evidenced in-repo.

sources.reference: scripts/experiments/zaremba-transitivity/check_transitivity.cu (source only; no results file); reviewer sieve check

claim_reviews.concerns: Commit the run output (per-prime orbit sizes or at least the summary block) — this is the project's own data-preservation rule.

claim_reviews.claim: The all-prime Dickson-classification argument is provisional: the generators have determinant -1, so SL2 framing is imprecise, and the exclusions must be reformulated in GL2/PGL2 or the even-word subgroup.
claim_reviews.evidence: The determinant observation is correct (det g_a = -1 for all a), and the page's self-demotion of its own algebraic argument — including a bulleted audit note asking for independent group-theoretic verification — is exactly the right posture. The revised argument's components are individually plausible (the resultant-based exceptional exclusion is a clean finite computation; the eigenline non-coincidence reductions are elementary), but this reviewer, like the page itself, does not certify the argument as a theorem: the Borel/Cartan steps as written still reason inside SL2 with det -1 generators, and step 2's nonsplit-Cartan case ends with 'reduces to the algebraic constraints above' without displaying the reduction.
claim_reviews.concerns: The o3-pro-revised argument has not been human-verified; the page says so plainly.

claim_reviews.claim: A local obstruction at any prime would yield infinitely many Zaremba counterexamples; no obstruction found through p = 17,389.
claim_reviews.evidence: The logical structure is standard (a missed residue class mod p blocks all d in that class), and the finite computation — modulo the missing log — is consistent with every other artifact in the project (e.g., zero uncovered denominators to 2.1e11 in the brute-force runs would be impossible under a small-prime obstruction).

overall_assessment: A well-hedged page whose framing survived its own audits: the certified content is the finite computation, the algebraic argument is explicitly provisional, and the determinant subtlety is disclosed rather than papered over. The arithmetic frame is exact (pi(17,389) = 2,000). The single real defect is that the finite computation — the page's one certified claim — has no committed run artifact, violating the project's own data-preservation convention.
recommendations: Commit the check_transitivity run output for the 2,000-prime sweep
Seek an independent group-theoretic review of the revised Dickson argument in the correct ambient group (GL2/PGL2 or even-word SL2)
certification_justification: Sound framing and exact arithmetic, but the sole certified claim lacks its artifact. Bronze; committing the run log would justify silver.
